StackType.rationale: PowerStackType.Counter. The sim has no StackType concept; Power.on_stack (powers.py:64-66) adds unconditionally, which is exactly what PowerCmd.ModifyAmount does (PowerCmd.cs:236 -- no StackType branch). Third-file citations, not hashed here.

AfterSideTurnEnd.issue: SLOT. AbstractModel.AfterSideTurnEnd is dispatched by Hook.AfterTurnEnd (Hook.cs:1267-1292), called ONCE for the whole enemy side (CombatManager.cs:1256) after every enemy has moved; the sim implements it with the PER-ENEMY slot on_enemy_turn_end (combat.py:341), which fires immediately after each enemy's own move. The sim HAS the side-scoped slot and does not use it here: on_enemy_side_end (combat.py:345). turn_structure gap G5 (the enemy side is per-enemy in the sim, per-side in the game) is the owning record and carries the identical `gap` verdict; not re-verdicted here per binding rule 3. DORMANT, and the dormancy is EXECUTED rather than asserted -- see `py audit/tools/power_slot_probes.py rosters` and `enemy-hook-order`. This is the sharpest per-creature case in the batch on paper and still dormant in fact. The Ovicopter lays up to 5 Tough Eggs (monsters/hive/ovicopter.py:24-25, _EGGS_PER_LAY=3 / _EGG_SLOTS=5) and each egg carries its own Hatch, and the eggs are inserted BEFORE the Ovicopter in the enemy list (ovicopter.py:137-150, display order [egg3, egg2, egg1, Ovicopter]) -- so in the sim egg 1's Hatch ticks before eggs 2-3 and the Ovicopter even move, where C# ticks all of them after every move. DORMANT because nothing reads another creature's Hatch amount: the hatch itself is the egg's own HATCH_MOVE (ovicopter.py:65-83) and the Ovicopter's lay condition counts live enemies, not Hatch (ovicopter.py:97-101 reads is_gone). Trigger: any effect keyed on a sibling's Hatch.

guards.issue: Folded into the AfterSideTurnEnd entry. Carried separately because with up to five simultaneous owners this is the one guard in this batch whose per-side vs per-creature reading genuinely differs, unlike the solo-owner units.

Same observable. `_tick` bypassing PowerCmd entirely is also the reason sign-aware-typing arm 2 is inert across the whole power set (the census's typing finding).
